subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in user-output file-permission policy for agent-created files, and what exact boundary and mode shape should it use?
rationale: The issue asks to intentionally widen local filesystem access for user-facing outputs while protecting private state, and that boundary cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design opt-in user-output policy
options.body: Define accepted modes or umask, the user-facing artifact boundary, private-state exclusions, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to concrete write bugs
options.body: Fix only specific current breakages such as outbound media or a particular tool path, without adding a broad config key yet.

options.title: Decline the config surface
options.body: Keep OS-level umask, ACLs, and deployment-specific repair tools as the operator-owned solution to avoid new security surface.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in user-output policy
recommendation.body: Define accepted modes or umask, the user-facing artifact boundary, private-state exclusions, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest path history is on the sandbox, apply_patch, and tools fs config boundaries that would define this security policy.
